caption: A redstone block next to its piston holds this TNT duplicator still; take the block away and it throws a lit TNT every 6 ticks (200 a minute) until you put it back, so a short pulse (the block away for 4 ticks) makes exactly one TNT. One TNT at a time lands 14 to 18 blocks away and explodes there, beyond the 7 blocks a blast can break, so it is safe standing right on the ground; left running free it is not (its TNT pile up 6 to 14 blocks away and the blasts reach it: it needs 4 blocks of air under it). Detail: the 12-block engine with a slime launcher (each TNT flung at 1 block per tick); one obsidian foot under the piston keeps the moving slimes off the grass (a slime frame resting on grass drags it). Measured on redsim at every kick angle: on grass the explosions are 14.2 to 18.5 blocks away, on obsidian 14.2; 0 machine blocks destroyed

The TNT duplicator: 86 lit TNT a minute, standing right on the ground, and no explosion ever touches it. Each TNT is thrown away at 1 block per tick and explodes on the ground 9 to 30 blocks off, where it breaks blocks, beyond the 7 blocks a blast reaches. It is two catalog parts: the 16-block duplicator engine, which makes one TNT each time its piston loses power for a moment, and a 6-block clock from the clock catalog (period 14 ticks) whose redstone block holds that piston and steps away for 4 ticks of every 14. Detail: robust over every kick angle on both grounds on redsim (and 64 runs with every TNT its own kick), 16 builds in the game; a period-10 clock gives 120 a minute but lands blasts 5.3 blocks away and fails about 1 game build in 30.

Every lit TNT explodes at exactly the same point in the air, almost 10 blocks up, bit for bit, and breaks nothing of the machine: a slow duplicator throws each TNT 4 blocks into a fence post that stops it over a little water channel, the current pushes it against a second fence post (that cancels the random sideways kick every TNT gets when it is lit), and 58 ticks after it was lit a slime piston under it launches it straight up, so it explodes at the top of its flight, more than 7 blocks from anything a blast could break. The precise TNT duplicator, for builds that need every TNT at one known spot (13.2 a minute); the fast one is tnt-clocked-22b.
